body.x: Owls Corp (CEO Han Seungwoo) announced its participation in CES 2025 in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 to 10 at the K-Startup Pavilion.

Owls Corp specializes in comprehensive solutions for the last-mile mobility sector. Its all-in-one platform covers rentals, leasing, maintenance, insurance, and secondhand transactions. Leveraging location-based services (LBS) and fleet management systems (FMS), the company collects and analyzes operational data to enhance safety and efficiency.

In addition, Owls Corp focuses on expanding the future mobility ecosystem through AI engine development and collaborations with global research institutions. The company aims to penetrate international markets while increasing the reach of its electric vehicle (EV) services for sustainable growth.

At CES 2025, Owls Corp will present AI-driven solutions developed from its extensive experience in the mobility sector. With seven years of expertise in the rental and leasing business, the company has continuously strengthened its data collection and processing capabilities to handle variables such as accidents. This culminated in developing an AI model for evaluating the residual value of electric two-wheeler batteries.

The AI solution analyzes collected data in real time, providing residual value assessments regardless of the vehicle’s location or operational status. This foundational technology can be extended to other mobility solutions, enabling broad application beyond two-wheelers.

Owls Corp has also automated essential management processes using proprietary algorithms, such as driver behavior evaluations and accident assessments. By integrating these specialized AI functions into a unified platform, the company has enhanced the competitiveness of its two-wheeler rental and leasing services, earning recognition as an industry leader.

Looking ahead, Owls Corp plans to apply its AI capabilities beyond mobility, offering valuation and assessment solutions across various industries. The company envisions significant growth opportunities by addressing diverse datasets and transforming them into actionable insights.

A company representative stated, “We have extensive experience collecting, processing, and transforming diverse datasets to meet client needs. For example, our solutions can be adapted for fire prevention systems, early warning mechanisms, or optimizing water quality management processes.”

The representative added, “Beyond mobility, vast opportunities exist to create new value through AI-driven assessments in global industries. True to the CES theme, Owls Corp aims to solve real-world challenges by leveraging data collection and connectivity, ultimately enhancing customer convenience and safety while expanding our business scope.”

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
